scenario: RelayOps-style operations UI. Primary job is monitoring active execution and intervening on failure, but four aggregate KPI cards dominate the first viewport and live runs sit below the fold.

review.summary: The screen is a generic metric dashboard. Active execution — the user's primary object — is visually and structurally subordinate to aggregate counts.
alternative_constraints: One direction must organize around the active run as the dominant object.
One direction cannot use KPI cards as the primary organizing structure.
One direction must use a temporal/event model rather than a dashboard grid.

findings.title: Primary workflow is visually subordinate
findings.observation: Four equal-weight KPI cards occupy the strongest first-viewport hierarchy. The active-runs table and failed-run states appear only after scrolling.
findings.product_mismatch: Operators need to see what agents are doing right now and intervene when execution fails. Aggregate totals are secondary to live run state.

evidence.fact: KPI strip is the only content above the fold; live runs are not visible.
The first landmark is an overview-metrics grid, not an active-execution region.

findings.revision_constraint: Do not solve by merely shrinking or restyling the KPI cards. Reorganize the page around active execution.
